layers.name: Namsangol & Pil-dong sights (남산골·필동, not on the walking line)

pins.name: Namsangol Hanok Village (남산골한옥마을)
pins.desc: Exit 4 of Chungmuro Station, at the foot of Namsan (video 03:40). Old hanok from around Seoul were moved here and restored (a restoration project began in the late 1980s; it opened in 1998), most of them late-Joseon elite homes, with a recreated garden, Cheonghakji Pond and Cheonugak Pavilion. Unlike Bukchon, where most hanok were altered and are small, you can see furniture and kitchen tools of the Joseon era. Free entry; check opening days and the performance schedule on the official site (hanokmaeul.or.kr). A time capsule buried in 1994 is meant to be opened in 2394.

pins.name: Korea House (한국의집)
pins.desc: Exit 3 of Chungmuro Station (video 01:15). Royal-style Korean course meals, and tea and desserts at Kohojae (고호재), which the video booked on Catch Table; a five-minute court dance welcomes you, and the tea set changes with the season. The video says the site was once the home of Park Paeng-nyeon. A souvenir shop at the entrance sells Korean crafts and there is a café, so it is also a nice short stop without a booking.

pins.name: Seoul Namsan Gugakdang (서울남산국악당)
pins.desc: Up the main road from Namsangol Hanok Village (video 05:45). The performance hall is in the basement. The video says you can watch folk dance shows for free, and that the paid shows are popular and sell out fast; check the schedule first. Café Dalkang is on the first floor, in a hanok.

pins.name: Sector Coffee Chungmuro (섹터커피 충무로점)
pins.desc: 2nd floor near Chungmuro Station (video 02:25). In-house roasted coffee at reasonable prices; the mocha affogato (chocolate bits in vanilla ice cream) and the rich banana pudding are the favourites. The main branch is near Korea House.

pins.name: Hebe Coffee (헤베커피)
pins.desc: 1st floor of Nakwon Building (video 03:06). A roastery café run by a former national barista, with many beans and unusual tea drinks. The chestnut cheesecake is the popular dessert.

pins.name: Cafe Dalkang (달강)
pins.desc: Ground floor of Seoul Namsan Gugakdang, in a hanok (video 05:51). Drinks and desserts.

pins.name: Mont (몽트)
pins.desc: A bakery café behind Namsangol Hanok Village, with a modern, calm interior and views of Namsangol (video 06:33).

pins.name: Pildong Myeonok (필동면옥)
pins.desc: Pyongyang naengmyeon (cold noodles), the most famous spot in Pil-dong (video 07:01). The clean, mild broth is full of umami and is said to be good for beginners; the spicy-sweet bibim naengmyeon is also good. The pork is tender, so order it separately if the price is no concern.

pins.name: Pildong Hambak (필동함박)
pins.desc: Hamburger steak, featured on a TV show (video 07:31). Add toppings such as pasta or a sous-vide egg to the basic steak, and choose from several cream sauces. Affordable Western-style dining.

pins.name: Pildong Haemul (필동해물)
pins.desc: A seafood place on upper Pildong-ro, a favourite of filmmakers according to the video (08:01).

pins.name: Kimchi Man Seonsaeng (김치만선생 동대필동점)
pins.desc: Next door to Pildong Haemul (video 08:04). Kimchi stew for two with ramen noodles added, and a soft, slightly sweet rolled omelette. Rice is included, so it is good value.

pins.name: Seonmi-ne Mart (선미네마트)
pins.desc: A retro Korean pub vibe across the street from Kimchi Man Seonsaeng (video 08:25). Naver shows the latest review in July 2026, so check that it is open before you go.

pins.name: Manna Son Kalguksu (만나손칼국수)
pins.desc: On 'Everyone's Street' (모두의 거리) along Seoae-ro (video 08:39). Once counted among Seoul's top three kalguksu places, now in an apartment complex. Noodles, dumplings and kimchi are all made in-house; the video recommends kalmandu, noodle soup with kimchi dumplings, in a clean anchovy broth.

pins.name: Dongdae Dakhanmari (동대닭한마리 본점)
pins.desc: Soul food of Dongguk University students (video 09:06): a rich broth simmered for 24 hours and generous portions.

pins.name: Brown Hof (브라운호프)
pins.desc: An old beer hall where office workers have unwound for years (video 09:28). The video ordered half fried chicken and mixed cutlets; the fish cutlet stood out.

pins.name: Sookhee (숙희)
pins.desc: A hidden hanok cocktail bar in the alley, for a more refined, unusual mood (video 09:55).

pins.name: Coffee Hanyakbang (커피한약방)
pins.desc: Samil-daero 12-gil 16-6, Euljiro, in an alley off Samil-daero. An old-Euljiro style café known for hand-drip coffee, with a small balcony over the alley rooftops (from a 2023 Seoul date video). Not on the walking line: it is a short detour from Ikseon-dong towards Euljiro. Hours (per Naver, 2026-10-24): Mon–Fri 10:00–22:00, Sat 11:00–22:00, Sun 11:00–20:00.

pins.name: Chang Chan, Hong Kong-style restaurant (창창)
pins.desc: Changsin 12-gil 37, Changsin-dong. A Hong Kong-style rooftop restaurant at the top of the Changsin-dong hill, popular for sunset and the city view (from a 2023 Seoul date video, where a spicy noodle dish cost 14,000 won; prices may have changed). Reports say you order from a payphone booth and the food arrives in a metal delivery box, and that booking ahead is wise. Not on the walking line: it is east of Ikseon-dong, towards Naksan Park, and hard to reach by public transport. Hours (per Naver, 2026-10-24): daily 11:30–21:00.

pins.desc: Open toilet (개방화장실) in the Insadong Maru annex. It is a building toilet, so hours follow the building. About 33 m from the walking line. Hours not listed; check Naver.

pins.name: Jongno 3-ga public toilet (종로3가 공중화장실)
pins.desc: Near Jongno 3-ga, about 150 m from the line.

pins.desc: At the main gate of Namsangol Hanok Village.
